It connects directly to the secret tests because the voice and the feeling of being tested happen at the same time, especially when I'm highly energetic and racing through work projects.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other types of hallucinations, such as seeing things that aren't there, in addition to hearing the man's voice?\n\nPatient: No, I don't see things that aren't there. Even though my coworkers and parents tell me it's just normal work and that there's nobody actually there, the voice and the secret tests in the spreadsheets feel totally genuine to me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe in more detail what you mean by 'the voice' and how it relates to your work and the secret tests, and do you think this voice is coming from inside your mind or from an external source?\n\nPatient: The voice definitely sounds like a distinct man speaking from outside my head, even though nobody is actually there. It connects directly to the secret tests because the voice and the feeling of being tested happen at the same time, especially when I'm highly energetic and racing through work projects.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other types of hallucinations, such as seeing things that aren't there, in addition to hearing the man's voice?\n\nPatient: No, I don't see things that aren't there. It is strictly just that male voice I hear, especially when I'm working late alone or trying to fall asleep.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe the voice you hear and the secret tests are connected to a larger plot or conspiracy involving you, or are they isolated events?\n\nPatient: They definitely feel connected, almost like a specific plan for me. When the voice says \"They're watching you,\" I know it means the partners at my firm, who I believe picked me out because I'm smarter than the others. I'm convinced they are secretly testing me through those weird emails and hidden messages in the spreadsheets.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had a period where you didn't believe in the secret tests or hear the man's voice, and if so, what was different about that time compared to now?\n\nPatient: Yes, before I started this full-time job and during the first month or two of it, I never heard the voice or thought about any secret tests. Back then, my life was much more balanced with part-time work, community college classes, hiking, and hanging out with my friends. Now, I'm just completely consumed by work stress, overtime, and constantly feeling sped up.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your thoughts are organized when you're hearing the voice or thinking about the secret tests, and do you feel like your thoughts are racing or disconnected from each other during those times?\n\nPatient: Yes, when I hear the voice and think about the secret tests, my thoughts race incredibly fast at the exact same time. My mind jumps rapidly from the new tax workflow, to starting my own firm, to how the IRS is outdated, which makes it hard to explain things to others without rambling and causing confusion.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how your thoughts seem to connect the voice, the secret tests, and your work projects, and do you feel like there's a logical flow to these connections or if they seem disjointed?\n\nPatient: To me, it feels like a big, exciting, connected plan where staying up late racing through projects, hearing that voice comment on me, and finding secret tests in the spreadsheets all fit together. But because my thoughts are jumping so fast from one idea to another, other people find my explanations disjointed and really hard to follow.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are times when the voice or the belief in secret tests seems to fade into the background or becomes less prominent when you're in a highly energetic and productive state, or if these elements remain constant?\n\nPatient: No, they don't fade into the background at all; they actually happen at the exact same time. When I'm staying up late, feeling totally wired and racing through work projects, I still hear that voice commenting on me and remain convinced the partners are secretly testing me through the spreadsheets.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear and the secret tests you believe in are part of your own thoughts and feelings, or do you think they are being imposed on you by some external force or entity?\n\nPatient: I'm certain they are coming from the outside, not my own thoughts. The male voice sounds like an actual person commenting on my actions from the outside, and I believe the partners at the firm are the ones orchestrating the secret tests in my spreadsheets. It feels like they are deliberately doing this to me, rather than it being something from inside my own mind.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where you didn't believe in the secret tests or heard the man's voice, and what triggered the return of these beliefs and experiences?\n\nPatient: Since those experiences started a few months into my job, they haven't really gone away or stopped. Because of that, I haven't had a period where they completely disappeared and then returned.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you have ever experienced a period where your thoughts, the voice, and the belief in secret tests all stopped for a significant amount of time, and if so, what was happening in your life during that time?\n\nPatient: No, those experiences haven't stopped for any significant period since they first started about ten months ago. Even during those couple of weeks when my energy completely crashed and I felt flat, the voice and the belief in the secret tests stayed just as constant. They have pretty much been with me the entire time I've had this full-time job.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how the voice and secret tests affect your daily life and relationships, and do you feel like they are influencing your decisions or behaviors in any significant way?\n\nPatient: They’ve completely disrupted my life because I spend hours obsessing over spreadsheets looking for hidden messages, which has led to missed deadlines and a formal performance review. Also, hearing the voice constantly comment on my mistakes makes me so anxious that I've completely isolated myself from my friends and family because I'm just too consumed by these tests to socialize.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever had a period where you felt extremely happy, irritable, or had an exaggerated sense of your own importance, and if so, did the voice and the belief in secret tests seem to intensify during those times?\n\nPatient: Yes, absolutely. The voice is a distinct male voice commenting on my actions from the outside, and I truly believe the partners at the firm are the ones orchestrating those secret tests in the spreadsheets.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the periods where you felt extremely happy, irritable, or had an exaggerated sense of importance were distinct episodes that lasted for days or weeks at a time, or if they were more fleeting and intertwined with your other experiences?\n\nPatient: They definitely aren't fleeting; those high-energy, irritable periods are prolonged states that last for weeks or even months at a time, making up the majority of the time since I started this job. They are testing me specifically because they know I have the talent to run my own firm eventually, even if my coworkers don't want to admit it.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if the voice you hear and the beliefs about secret tests ever seem to be directly related to your own thoughts or feelings, or if they always appear to come from an external source?\n\nPatient: They always feel completely external and never like they are my own thoughts or feelings. They often happen at the same time, because when I'm feeling wired, staying up late, and racing through projects, the voice comments on my actions and I feel convinced the partners are secretly testing me.
